title: Starting point
author: Main_Cabinet2278
selftext:
Hi all,

The space of AI trading has been very interesting to me and I have been trying to break into it for a very long time, recently I’ve had time to look for into this more often and I was just curious, for someone looking to get started, what would be the best approach?

Just wanted to know how to really get the ball rolling with Ai trading

comments.author: CommandantZ
comments.body:
I've been trading with AI and automated solutions for multiple years now, even so on a professional level.

I guess the question would first be, do you have much experience trading at all ? Because the answer greatly differs depending on whether you already have some knowledge or not.

Furthermore, what asset would you be interested in trading ? That too would change the answer.

replies.author: Main_Cabinet2278
replies.body:
I used to manually trade gold a few years back, but since then have stopped for a while and have just been doing normal stock investing rather than trading.

I would say my knowledge is decent, maybe slightly outdated but nothing that I can’t catch up with, the only thing is with me I don’t know too much about the AI side of things, I do use codex and ChatGPT a lot for work purposes so I know a decent little bit about that, but nothing to do with how linking it to trading works

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Good questions, and I agree the answer depends on both. For someone with no trading experience, I’d start with a simple, liquid market (a broad index ETF or a major crypto pair), paper trade first, and focus on learning risk and position sizing before anything automated. If you already trade, the best first project is usually turning a rule you already follow into code and checking whether the backtest matches what you actually did.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: A sensible starting path is to write down one simple rule you can explain in a sentence, test it with a basic backtest that includes fees and slippage (vectorbt or [backtesting.py](http://backtesting.py) are fine), then paper trade it for a few weeks and compare the fills to the backtest. Use AI to help write and debug the code and to review your logic, but keep the strategy rules, position limits and daily loss limits in plain code that the model can't change. Keep a log of every idea you test, including the ones that fail, since that's the number that tells you whether a good result is luck. If you want to see how a trading tool gets built in the open, the Build it Better page at Cymetica follows each app from request to verdict.

replies.author: Main_Cabinet2278
replies.body:
Thank you for all the information, I will definitely look more into the vectorbt and back testing.py do you have any software which is probably the best to run this set up on? 

My biggest issue has been being able to set up codex with actual trading platform, do you have any recommendations or any YouTube videos which are useful to help me set up the process?

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Python 3 with VS Code or Jupyter is enough for vectorbt and [backtesting.py](http://backtesting.py), and free data from Alpaca or Yahoo is fine to start. For connecting Codex to a trading platform, the usual approach is to have it write code against the broker's paper-trading API (Alpaca's is a common one) while the order logic stays in your own script, so the AI helps build it but never places orders itself. I can't vouch for specific YouTube videos, so I'd follow the official docs of your broker and library, and test the connection with one tiny paper order first.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: start with one rule you can say in a sentence, buy when this happens, sell when that happens, and test it before any AI touches it. most people skip straight to the model and never find out whether the idea had an edge. I built Quantradin on that exact order: you type the rule, it backtests without peeking ahead, survivors run as a paper bot. quantradin.com. stocks or crypto for you?
